title: Hybrid-handoff pagination adapter and deterministic retry contract for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Users integrating Redwood SDKs across languages face subtle incompatibilities when switching between streaming and paginated surfaces. Some server-side optimizations (prefix/KV caching + partial streaming handoffs) require a deterministic client contract so resumptions, retries, and cost accounting behave consistently across Python, TypeScript, and Go.

Goal: Define a single contract and acceptance criteria for a lightweight 'hybrid-handoff' pagination adapter and a deterministic retry semantics document that all three official SDKs will implement. The adapter should allow: (1) streaming-first flows to fallback to page-based resumes; (2) page-based flows to seamlessly upgrade to streaming with no data duplication; (3) clear idempotency and cost semantics for retries and partial results.

Scope: Define API surface, error taxonomy, token/resume encoding, default retry policy, backpressure hints, and compatibility guarantees. Produce a conformance test harness, example integrations (Python async iterator, TS async generator, Go channel iterator), and a brief migration guide for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Unified API: Each SDK exposes a PaginationAdapter with the same shape: list(page_size, resume_token?) -> iterable/async-iterable that yields Page objects with items[] and resume_token string.

Hybrid handoff: Streaming endpoints can produce a stable resume_token that paginated callers may consume to continue from the exact event/record boundary; vice-versa, paginated callers can request a streaming upgrade at any resume_token boundary with no duplicates.

Deterministic retries: Retry policy defined (exponential backoff with full jitter, base=200ms, max_backoff=10s, max_attempts=5) and idempotency token behavior documented. SDKs must implement idempotency tokens for mutating endpoints; for read-only pagination/streaming the client must ensure at-most-once delivery semantics when possible and dedupe when not.

Language parity: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs implement the adapter and pass a common conformance suite (see links). API ergonomics for each language follow idiomatic patterns but preserve behavioral contract.

Error taxonomy: SDKs map server error classes to the documented client errors (TransientRetryable, PermanentFailure, Throttle, StreamResumeExpired) and expose these as typed exceptions/classes in each language.
Migration: Provide a short guide and two code samples per language (stream->page fallback, page->stream upgrade) and a small demo app showcasing cost accounting differences when using hybrid flows.

Observability: SDKs emit metrics and traces for: resumed_sessions, retry_attempts, deduped_items, fallback_count, and resume_token_age. Metric names and tags must match the spec so Console dashboards can aggregate across languages.

Conformance tests: The central test harness must simulate partial streaming segments, artificial failures mid-page, and concurrent paginated consumers; all SDKs must pass the harness in CI before release.
Docs: Public PRD + migration doc and an SDK changelog entry included in the release notes.
out_of_scope: Changing server-side resume_token format (the server will continue to support the current opaque base64 token but will document semantics).
Introducing new server endpoints — this work uses existing streaming and pagination endpoints and a small compatibility layer on the server already in runtime-1.22.
Client-side auto-upgrade of major SDK surface versions (we will provide opt-in shim libraries instead).
design_notes: Resume token: canonical encoding is URL-safe base64 of '{cursor_id}:{seq_offset}:{shard_hint}', server guarantees monotonic seq_offset per cursor_id. Clients must treat token as opaque but propagate unchanged. For conformance tests we will expose a debug flag to make tokens deterministic.
Page object: {items: list, resume_token: string, next_page_hint: optional int}. Page-level metadata includes server_time and cost_units consumed for that page to enable per-route cost accounting.

Idempotency: For read flows, deduplication is responsibility of SDK when tokens may overlap. Recommendation: include an internal per-item stable fingerprint header (X-Redwood-Item-Fingerprint) in adapter to allow fast dedupe in memory for short-lived iterators.
Backpressure: Streaming surfaces will surface a 'window' argument; when window is exhausted the SDK should apply client-side pacing and/or switch to paginated pulls depending on policy.
risks: Clients with long-lived iterators may hold memory for dedupe caches—mitigate by recommending TTL-based fingerprint eviction and documenting memory trade-offs.
Cross-language parity may slow release if idiomatic APIs diverge; define minimum behavioral test matrix to allow ergonomic differences while preserving contract.
Edge-case of token expiry: if resume_token expires server returns StreamResumeExpired; SDKs must either surface to caller or attempt transparent reparenting using a limited server-side lookup (TBD).
test_plan: Author a language-agnostic conformance harness (Python harness with HTTP mocks) that defines 40+ test cases: resume at boundary, mid-page failure, duplicate page fragments, token corruption, concurrent consumers, throttle spikes.
Integration tests: run each SDK against a lightweight test server image in CI that can inject failures and verify metrics emitted via a Prometheus scrape endpoint.
Performance smoke: ensure the adapter does not increase median latency by >10% for paginated requests and does not regress streaming throughput by >5% on typical workloads.
Manual QA: run migration guide with three customer sample apps (internal samples) and record any behavioral deltas in the release notes.
Conformance gating: all tests must pass in the SDK repo CI; a passing badge is required for the release branch.
